t: A family of tiny Raspberry Pi add-ons with sound, a screen and four buttons.
steps: Buy the board you want from Pimoroni or a maker store.
Get a Raspberry Pi with a 40-pin header, an SD card and a power supply.
Install Raspberry Pi OS on the SD card with Raspberry Pi Imager.
Press the Pirate Audio board onto the Pi's 40-pin header.
Boot the Pi and run the Pimoroni installer from the getting started tutorial.
Reboot and look for the music player on the little screen.
Open the music player page from a computer on the same network and play a song.
Try the clip recorder example on the Dual Mic board.
meta: Open Code. From $23.95. A few stores.
